title: Culture Atlas — Gossip Mode public-source research

scope.additional_city_reason: BAK appeared as a suggested research subject in the supplied screenshot.
scope.selection: Purposeful sample of public disputes and outcomes; not a statistical sample or full institution audit.

integration.reason: The institution master list and application data were not supplied.

methodology.claim_handling: Attribute allegations to their source; distinguish a documented event from proof of the allegation.
methodology.status_handling: Status refers to the latest located evidence, not continuous live monitoring. Unknown current outcomes are explicit.
methodology.response_handling: No institution was contacted. 'Not located' does not mean an institution refused to respond.
methodology.reviews_handling: Dated, self-reported employee and visitor accounts are leads. Employment is unverified; no aggregate score, representative inference, or automatic institution flag is used.
access_limits: Some social posts linked by public sources could not be retrieved; no systematic Instagram or Facebook comment analysis was performed.
Wayback snapshot retrieval failed; historical changes rely on dated public documents and reporting.
Registration-only article sections and private groups were not accessed.
No independent legal judgment is inferred from a campaign or employee allegation.
Glassdoor profile, role, locale, and mirror pages can display different excerpts or no reviews. Related excerpts are not attributed to the host page's main reviewer; no login-only text was used.
methodology.employee_review_selection: Public profile matching and dated excerpt sampling on Kununu and Glassdoor; positive, mixed, and critical accounts retained. Non-exhaustive and not representative; distinct account records do not establish distinct people. Two KW accounts are limited to titles and metadata, explicitly marked; other new records contain narrative excerpts.

required_card_fields: Institution and exact workforce or sponsor
display_suggestions.principle: Funding status, workplace conditions, and programming disputes should remain separate dimensions.

source_channels.name: Union and worker sources
source_channels.use: Identify pay, contractor, staffing, and safety disputes; search the same source for later agreements.
source_channels.caution: A union statement proves what the union said; disputed allegations still need attribution.

source_channels.name: Artist letters and campaign archives
source_channels.use: Follow demands, withdrawals, board conflicts, and campaign outcomes in participants' own words.
source_channels.caution: Keep signatories' accusations separate from verified decisions.

source_channels.name: Funding campaign groups
source_channels.use: Find sponsorship disputes, FOI documents, public actions, and exit campaigns.
source_channels.caution: Record advocacy position and competing explanations for a sponsor exit.

source_channels.name: Official decisions and hearings
source_channels.use: Check deadlines, court outcomes, policy disputes, and formal government responses.
source_channels.caution: Record the exact issue decided; procedural findings are not wider ethical verdicts.

source_channels.name: Arts and museum reporting
source_channels.use: Find institutional replies and follow-ups across cities and languages.
source_channels.caution: Distinguish reporting from commentary and note partial article access.

source_channels.name: Worker and visitor reviews
source_channels.use: Discover dated employee and visitor questions about pay, workload, contracts, management, access, and visitor treatment.
source_channels.caution: Do not turn review ratings or isolated experiences into a verified misconduct flag.

source_channels.name: Independent criticism and interviews
source_channels.use: Find questions about class, exclusion, artistic freedom, and precarity that press releases miss.
source_channels.caution: Opinion and participant interpretations remain attributed.

source_channels.name: Arts gossip columns
source_channels.use: Spot institutional developments that warrant a document search.
source_channels.caution: Use original evidence for allegations; this research did not extract personal gossip.

source_channels.name: Dated documents and archive comparisons
source_channels.use: Preserve dated evidence of staffing decisions, exhibition outcomes, and funding assessments.
source_channels.caution: Wayback retrieval failed in this pass; no archive change reconstruction is claimed.

cases.title: BP funding and information disclosure

facts.text: A £50m, ten-year BP partnership was announced for the museum masterplan.

attributed_claims.text: Culture Unstained opposes continued fossil-fuel sponsorship.

response.text: The museum said BP funding supports transformation and continued public access.

outcome.text: July 2026 ICO ruling upheld some withholding, required release of already-public material, and found response-deadline breaches.

limits: The ICO ruling concerns information handling; it is not a ruling that BP sponsorship is unlawful.
cases.follow_up: Check current contract disclosures and compliance with the ICO notice.

cases.title: Tobacco sponsorship ended; cause contested

facts.text: Japan Tobacco International sponsorship ended in September 2025.

attributed_claims.text: Culture Unstained credited government intervention.

response.text: The museum called it an independent board decision; DCMS denied forcing it.

outcome.text: The relationship ended; explanations for the decision differ.

limits: The campaign's causal explanation is disputed.
cases.follow_up: Preserve the exit date and separate it from remaining sponsorships.

cases.title: BP exit is a partial sponsorship change

facts.text: The museum group confirmed its BP partnership ended on 31 August 2026.

attributed_claims.text: Culture Unstained described the exit as a campaign victory.

response.text: The group said the agreed term expired, disputing reports of a 2028 end date.

outcome.text: BP tie ended; Adani Green Energy remained associated with a gallery in the latest report.

limits: A BP exit does not establish that all contested sponsorship ended.
cases.follow_up: Track each sponsor separately and retain competing accounts of the exit.

cases.title: Pay and conditions dispute; voluntary exit concerns

facts.text: PCS and Prospect members struck at London sites in September 2026.
October reporting described a voluntary exit scheme across V&A sites.

attributed_claims.text: Unions sought better pay and conditions; PCS warned cuts could increase workloads.

response.text: V&A says staff receive London Living Wage, have water and breaks, and its offer is affordable.

outcome.text: The dispute remained unresolved in reporting dated 6 October.

limits: This record concerns PCS/Prospect; contractor guards' UVW disputes involve a separate bargaining context.
Living Wage accreditation and actual pay levels are distinct questions.
cases.follow_up: Check the next union and museum updates for a settlement.

cases.title: Pay dispute ended with an agreement

facts.text: Prospect members voted for industrial action over pay.

attributed_claims.text: Prospect argued the offer fell short of workers' needs.

response.text: No separate museum reply was located in the outcome report.

outcome.text: Staff accepted a 3.5% pay increase and ended action by April 2026.

limits: The agreement date is less precise than the report date.
cases.follow_up: Show the settlement alongside the original grievance.

cases.title: Pigeon branding attribution dispute

facts.text: May Wild Studio publicly challenged the museum's pigeon branding.

attributed_claims.text: The designers alleged similarities to their earlier Coo Pigeon design.

response.text: London Museum denied copying and described independent development.

outcome.text: No adjudication or settlement was located.

limits: A copying allegation is not an established infringement.
cases.follow_up: Seek the original design chronology and any legal outcome.

cases.title: Layoffs, bargaining, and a new contract

facts.text: The museum cut 20 jobs in February 2025.

attributed_claims.text: The union objected to notice and representation around the cuts.

response.text: The museum cited financial pressure and operating costs.

outcome.text: Union staff ratified a second contract by 2 October 2026.

limits: Contract ratification does not show that laid-off employees were reinstated or every grievance resolved.
cases.follow_up: Obtain agreement terms and the separate layoffs grievance outcome.

cases.title: Proposed layoffs and later UAW agreement

facts.text: Reporting described 47 planned layoffs; the museum announced roughly 10% workforce reduction.

attributed_claims.text: UAW and DC37 challenged the proposed cuts and bargaining process.

response.text: Leadership cited deficits, rising costs, and weak attendance recovery.

outcome.text: UAW-represented staff ratified a second contract by 2 October 2026.

limits: The planned 47 is not a verified final dismissal count.
The UAW outcome does not establish the outcome for every DC37 member.
cases.follow_up: Check final workforce numbers and the separate DC37 outcome.

cases.title: October strike averted by ratification

facts.text: Union members had authorised action and set an October strike deadline.

attributed_claims.text: Workers sought stronger pay and employment provisions.

response.text: A separate current museum statement was not located.

outcome.text: Members ratified an agreement on 4 October, averting the 5 October strike.

limits: Ratification is the outcome of this bargaining dispute, not a general workplace rating.
cases.follow_up: Link the public ratified contract when available.

cases.title: Kanders board campaign and resignation

facts.text: A public scholars' and artists' letter called for Warren Kanders to leave the board.

attributed_claims.text: Campaigners opposed his Safariland connection and demanded trustee accountability.

response.text: The museum confirmed his departure and thanked him for his support.

outcome.text: Kanders resigned on 25 July 2019; artists rescinded withdrawal requests.

limits: This is a historical board departure, not evidence of current trusteeship.
cases.follow_up: Use it as a documented campaign outcome and review today's board separately.

cases.title: Staff dismissals under a dress code

facts.text: Three employees were fired after wearing keffiyehs under a new dress policy.

attributed_claims.text: Staff opposed the policy through a petition, walkout, and protest.

response.text: The museum said political expression could alienate visitors and cited personnel privacy.

outcome.text: No reinstatement or final personnel outcome was located.

limits: Dismissals are reported; a legal finding of discrimination was not established.
cases.follow_up: Check later staff, museum, and any public legal records.

cases.title: First union contract after bargaining pressure

facts.text: Workers participated in collective bargaining and coordinated strike authorisation.

attributed_claims.text: Union members pressed for higher pay and improved conditions.

response.text: A separate current museum reply was not located.

outcome.text: Workers ratified their first contract by 2 October 2026.

limits: Do not keep a threatened strike marked active after ratification.
cases.follow_up: Add the signed agreement and implementation milestones.

cases.title: Winter strikes and an unfinished protocol

facts.text: CGT documented winter mobilisation and an April 2026 wait for a protocol.

attributed_claims.text: Workers sought action on working conditions and staffing.

response.text: At a June Senate hearing, management described a pending protocol and conditional recruitment.

outcome.text: Management said physical strikes had stopped; the protocol remained pending in June.

limits: No October settlement was verified; absence of physical strikes differs from a signed resolution.
cases.follow_up: Locate the final protocol and recruitment implementation.

cases.title: Closure-related strike resolved in 2024

facts.text: A roughly 100-day dispute concerned staff protections during renovation closure.

attributed_claims.text: Workers sought assurances about redeployment.

response.text: The culture ministry announced a protocol with FO and CFDT.

outcome.text: Agreement on 29 January 2024 ended that dispute.

limits: Renovation closure is not evidence that this strike continues.
cases.follow_up: Check implementation of redeployment commitments during renovation.

cases.title: Court rejected a request to remove artwork

facts.text: A legal challenge sought removal of a Miriam Cahn painting.

attributed_claims.text: Applicants challenged its suitability for display.

response.text: The institution contextualised the work and took precautions regarding minors.

outcome.text: Conseil d'État rejected the removal request on 14 April 2023.

limits: The ruling concerns this display and its context.
cases.follow_up: Keep the judgment linked rather than reducing the episode to a censorship label.

cases.title: Goldin dispute alongside a completed exhibition

facts.text: Nan Goldin's November opening speech prompted protest and an institutional response.

attributed_claims.text: Goldin later accused the museum of censoring an added slide.

response.text: The museum disputed that account and said her studio removed the slide after discussion.

outcome.text: The exhibition continued and closed on 6 April 2025.

limits: A disputed slide removal is distinct from cancellation of the exhibition.
The newspaper also contains commentary; its judgments are not adopted here.
cases.follow_up: Link original interview and slide correspondence if made public.

cases.title: Funding dispute and a procedural court remand

facts.text: Berlin declined further funding; an interim application failed in December 2023.

attributed_claims.text: Oyoun contested the funding withdrawal.

response.text: The Senate said there was no enforceable funding entitlement.

outcome.text: Oyoun reported a July 2024 constitutional remand; final restoration was not verified.

limits: A remand is not final restoration of funding.
Current homepage indexing mentions 2025–2026 foundation support; direct page access failed (S34).
cases.follow_up: Locate the post-remand decision and current operational funding.

cases.title: Bruguera performance ended after disruption

facts.text: Protesters disrupted Tania Bruguera's scheduled reading performance.

attributed_claims.text: Protesters challenged the platform given to participants and the absence of Palestinian voices.

response.text: The museum said Bruguera decided to stop after the disruption.

outcome.text: The performance ended before its scheduled 11 February finish.

limits: Disruption by protesters does not establish that the museum censored the artist.
cases.follow_up: Preserve the artist decision and museum account as attributed.

cases.title: ING sponsorship challenged by climate campaigners

facts.text: XR documented an April 2025 protest targeting ING sponsorship.
A 2023 museum disclosure identifies ING as main sponsor.

attributed_claims.text: XR criticised ING's fossil-fuel financing and sought an end to the tie.

response.text: No direct museum reply to this protest was located.

outcome.text: The sponsorship's October 2026 status was not verified.

limits: Campaign language is not a legal finding against ING.
A 2023 disclosure cannot alone establish today's sponsorship.
cases.follow_up: Check the latest signed agreement or current institutional sponsor disclosure.

cases.title: Programming guidelines drew parliamentary questions

facts.text: New programming guidelines prompted questions in the Dutch parliament.

attributed_claims.text: The questions raised concerns about exclusions tied to international crimes.

response.text: The minister defended programming autonomy within the law.

outcome.text: Official answers were published on 12 May 2026.

limits: Parliamentary questions do not establish unlawful discrimination.
The venue is distinct from the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra.
cases.follow_up: Get the original guideline text and monitor actual programming decisions.

cases.title: Shell sponsorship ended in 2018

facts.text: The museum's 18-year Shell sponsorship ended in August 2018.

attributed_claims.text: Climate campaigners had opposed the relationship.

response.text: Museum and Shell described a mutual decision.

outcome.text: The reported sponsorship ended; its cause should remain attributed.

limits: This source does not support marking Shell as a current sponsor.
cases.follow_up: Review current donors separately from this historical exit.

cases.title: Subcontracted visitor-service strike

facts.text: SUT announced a strike by subcontracted information and mediation workers.

attributed_claims.text: The union opposed staffing and hours reductions.

response.text: The museum linked two Retiro information-post cuts to heat conditions and described planned mediation expansion.

outcome.text: Mediation staff resumed on 24 June; the information-service dispute had no verified final settlement.

limits: The teams have different strike outcomes.
Planned October mediation posts were not verified as implemented.
cases.follow_up: Check each contractor's settlement and the October tender implementation.

cases.title: Union reports reversal of contractor hours cuts

facts.text: SUT linked a strike to reductions in Magmacultura staff hours.

attributed_claims.text: Workers sought restoration of hours and pay.

response.text: An independent employer reply was not located.

outcome.text: SUT reported an agreement restoring hours and retroactive pay.

limits: Only the union outcome account was located; exact agreement date is unconfirmed.
This is not a judicial finding.
cases.follow_up: Get the written agreement and employer confirmation.

cases.title: Contractor agreement before a planned strike

facts.text: SUT described an agreement with Magmacultura before a planned 11 December strike.

attributed_claims.text: Workers sought guaranteed hours and predictable schedules.

response.text: No separate employer or venue statement was located.

outcome.text: The union reports an agreement on 9 December 2025.

limits: The source concerns this contractor workforce, not every Fundación la Caixa employee.
cases.follow_up: Check schedule commitments and compliance with the agreement.

cases.title: Structural subsidy loss and Basecamp rebuilding

facts.text: BAK says it lost all structural subsidies in 2025 and rebuilt as BAK Basecamp.

attributed_claims.text: The published assessment praised artistic quality but raised audience reach and financial dependence concerns.

response.text: BAK describes collective rebuilding with support from several named funds.

outcome.text: Its current statement sets out Basecamp activity for 2026 and plans through 2028.

limits: The documents do not establish censorship as the cause of all funding loss.
Listed supporters are not independently certified as ethical funders.
cases.follow_up: Compare current funding with 2024–2025 accounts and funders' own disclosures.

evidence_rules: Reviewers' roles and employment status are self-described; no employment or identity verification.
A posting date does not establish when the employment experience occurred.
Anonymous accounts and repeat updates are not independent corroboration.
Positive accounts remain alongside concerns; a sample of reviews is not an ethical or workplace rating.
No aggregate ratings, review totals, salary estimates, demographic scores, or CEO labels used.
Glassdoor Recommend, CEO approval, and Business Outlook controls are not interpreted as reviewer votes.
Related-review excerpts have an explicit locator and no invented standalone permalink.
Parent-group and contractor accounts cannot be assigned to an individual museum without site evidence.
Earlier reviews do not establish that grievances continued after a later union agreement.
No institution or reviewer contacted; no login-only, private-group, or personal-identity material accessed.
Title-only accounts are identified separately; category headings or aggregate ratings are not translated into specific allegations.
